In the context of world history, the longest war is widely considered to be the Reconquista, which spanned 781 years [d1][d5][d6][d9]. The Reconquista was fought by Spanish and Portuguese forces against the Muslim rulers of the Iberian Peninsula, beginning around 711 CE and ending in 1492 CE when Granada fell to Ferdinand II and Isabella I [d1]. Other historically long conflicts include the Roman-Germanic Wars (708 years) and the Anglo-French Wars (706 years) [d1]. In a different scope, the Afghanistan War is identified as the longest war in U.S. history, lasting nearly two decades and costing close to $1 trillion [d7][d8]. Additionally, some sources use "longest war" to refer to specific regional conflicts, such as the Iran-Iraq War (1980–1988) [d3] or the Burma campaign of World War II [d4], though these are not comparable in duration to the Reconquista on a world-historical scale.
